metadata.description: Ten-item self-report measure of generalized confidence in initiating and managing actions across different situations.
metadata.intended_use: Research assessment of general self-efficacy in adolescents and adults; this reference record does not include item wording.
metadata.name_origin: General Self-Efficacy Scale, often abbreviated GSE; generalized refers to cross-situational rather than task-specific efficacy.
metadata.development_history: The English source record cites Schwarzer and Jerusalem's 1995 measurement chapter and provides language-version resources.
metadata.measurement_rationale: General self-efficacy concerns perceived capability to cope with a broad range of demands, rather than ability in one task.
metadata.interpretation_notes: The source guidance excludes children below age 12; use the source scoring and language-specific evidence and do not treat the score as competence proof.
metadata.notes: Link-only record. The FU Berlin author site hosts the scale and translations, but an explicit licence permitting public redistribution of item wording was not verified in the reviewed pages.

target_populations.group_name: General population including adults and adolescents
target_populations.notes: Author-hosted source says persons below age 12 should not be tested.

versions.source_citation: Schwarzer, R., & Jerusalem, M. (1995). Generalized Self-Efficacy scale. In Measures in health psychology: A user's portfolio (pp. 35-37).

source_documents.title: General Self-Efficacy Scale English source page
source_documents.license_name: Use terms not explicit on reviewed source; link only
source_documents.permission_basis: The author-hosted page describes the English form and translations, but the reviewed page does not explicitly grant public redistribution of item text. This is a catalog rights-status flag, not a use ban.

metadata.notes: The source reports 10 items, a four-point response scale, and a total range of 10-40. Population guidance: intended for adults/adolescents; do not administer below age 12 without source review.
